claims.statement: The contribution-settings index covers FPT/GHES/GHEC and six children for overview, viewing, private visibility, GHES sharing, troubleshooting and timeline details. The index is navigation, not completeness of displayed work or permission for disclosure.

Across products, Profile, Contribution settings, Private contributions shows or hides anonymized activity from private and internal repositories. This is a disclosure preference, not a repository-visibility or access-control change and not proof that metadata cannot disclose activity patterns.

Achievement visibility and individual hiding are gated by hide-individual-achievements, available FPT/GHEC only. Settings permits showing or hiding all achievements; individual profile badges can be hidden with the eye control and are described as then visible only to the user. Actual observer behavior still needs verification.

Connecting GHES activity to a cloud profile is governed by the linked Privacy Statement and requires the enabling user to agree to Terms of Service. Source review does not supply that human agreement or legal clearance.

Enterprise owners must enable GitHub Connect and contribution sharing before users connect profiles. FPT/GHEC versions direct users to the GHES procedure; the prerequisite is not satisfied by account existence or a navigation link.

The GHES sign-in instruction names Enterprise Cloud twice despite surrounding text describing a GHES-to-cloud connection. Preserve this source inconsistency rather than silently repairing it or treating it as a verified two-environment sign-in procedure.

The GHES flow opens Settings, GitHub Connect, Connect to GitHub.com, reviews requested resources and Authorize, then Send my contribution counts to PLATFORM and Update contributions. Authorization and disclosure are separate approved writes, not read-only assessment.

The ghecom-github-connect feature gates the data-residency destination wording to GHES >=3.12. The reusable button still names GitHub.com and the source has an unusual elsif ghes conditional; source-variable/rendered destination agreement remains unverified. Contribution counts do not transfer repository contents, ownership or authenticated authorship.

Across products, Profile, Contribution settings, Activity overview changes whether a contribution-type overview is presented. Enabling it is optional disclosure, not a productivity metric, complete activity inventory or evidence of resource access.
Qualifying commits may take up to 24 hours to appear; missing recent graph entries alone do not prove missing commits or failed repository writes. Delay does not waive other qualification criteria.

Attribution requires a commit-author email linked to the account, with cloud-provided noreply additionally described for FPT/GHEC. The .patch view's From field reflects the configured author address, not authenticated account identity or cryptographic proof.

The guide says adding the exact historical author email rebuilds the graph, and removal or movement to another account removes historical display; readding can restore attribution without mailbox access, with up to 24 hours refresh and then support escalation. This is not verification of mailbox control, authority to attach another person's address or proven account recovery.

For FPT/GHEC managed users, additional emails cannot be added even if the IdP contains several; only commits using the primary IdP email can associate. Generic local addresses such as computer.local cannot be added and linked; these exceptions qualify the generic historical-email advice.

Counting commits requires default branch or gh-pages for project-site repositories. A proposed PR merge or default-branch change can affect eligibility, but changing the default affects all collaborators and needs approved workflow-impact review. Graph presentation does not justify bypassing merge controls.
Fork commits do not count unless changes are merged into the parent through a PR. An opened PR is not a completed merge, nor evidence of parent access or preservation of all historical work.

The timeline commit-count link opens commit details. Rewritten history may cause author and committer dates to differ; the source's git show pretty=fuller example is read-only diagnostic data, not an instruction to rewrite history.

The guide proposes date-specific UTC since/until URL queries for author versus commit dates, but its example uses +0900 timestamps and substitutes their calendar dates into UTC bounds without discussing conversion. Timezone and boundary equivalence must be independently verified; a query returning no commits is not proof of absence.

The author URL parameter and displayed dates are search inputs, not proof of authenticated authorship. Missing profile history has other qualifying/visibility causes; no example identity, personal address or real assessment detail is collected.

Viewing a graph requires understanding what qualifies as a contribution. The resolved reusable states author-email linkage is necessary; graph appearance is not a complete repository census or quality/effort measurement.

The profile calendar supports clicking a day or Shift-selecting a range, capped at one month; a larger selection displays only one month. A selected long interval must not be reported as full-range coverage.
The Contribution activity timeline starts with recent work and permits Show more activity or selecting older years. Paging and year filters are navigation, not exhaustive historical retrieval.

GHES contribution counts can be sent to a cloud profile only when the enterprise owner enables unified contributions. Counts and linked instructions are not proof of a connected account or successful export.
